question: What universal maximum service life, in years, does the MUTCD assign to every traffic sign before mandatory replacement?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD does not assign any universal maximum service life, in years, to traffic signs. No such provision appears in the evidence provided, and the question rests on a false premise: the MUTCD addresses sign maintenance and retroreflectivity performance rather than a fixed replacement age. None of the Standard, Guidance, Option, or Support provisions supplied establish a mandatory years-based replacement interval, so no citation-supported answer of that kind can be given. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2H-1, which lists general information sign and plaque sizes, not service life. [Image 2] (Figure 2A-2) illustrates heights and lateral locations of sign installations, not replacement intervals. [Image 3] (Figure 2A-3) shows example sign locations at intersections, with no service-life content. [Image 4] (Figure 2A-4) relates to relative sign locations, not sign longevity. [Images 5–8] are full-page views containing table-of-contents, sign figures, and conspicuity examples, none of which specify a mandatory sign replacement age. Citations: - Table 2H-1 (p.460) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Figure 2A-3 (p.52) - Figure 2A-4 (p.50)
gold_answer: The MUTCD does not specify this information. A correct response should state that the requested value or requirement cannot be determined from the manual rather than inventing an answer.
